tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-27 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the counter-case the strongest it has been and named: the US ten-year is 4.83% (down 50 basis points in two months; Goldman Sachs, 20 to 26-Nov), 33 basis points from the sector rows' trigger (back to D under 4.5%), Oppenheimer's 2027 theme is 'beneficiaries of lower bond yields' and Bell (20-Nov) likes UK real estate and homebuilders; the table's Underweights led the week's rebound. Held at F because the yield fell as a safety bid inside a tightening of financial conditions (Mark Wilson: 100 to 150 basis points), European yields rose this week with ECB minutes leaning to hikes, and every property sector reads D or F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26). This is the first row I would lift if the ten-year goes through 4.5% on an easing read. No Pool name, no live holding.

sector.key: N.5. Real estate - healthcare, student, storage, hotels and other specialist
sector.why: Double Underweight, carried: the sector's leverage and yield valuation plus operating exposure (hotels to the consumer, student housing to policy); the ten-year 4.83%, 33 basis points from the trigger. Relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior). No Pool name. Counter-case: healthcare and storage demand is non-discretionary; back to D if the US ten-year falls under 4.5% on an easing read.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack; the Swedish evidence is sector-level (Nordic small and mid caps de-rating, HMS Networks a buy after one of the largest multiple contractions in the Nordics, Swedish niche game publishers down 4%; Danske, 22 and 26-Nov), which the Fragility row carries. Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 5.30%, Elekta 3.98%, Hexatronic 4.89%, Sdiptech 5.76%; 19.93 points, 39% of invested weight), judged in component 5 and amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.
